title: charts(private): add LTS runtime tag selection + enable recommended LTS alerts by default
author: Sahana Iyer
description:
Context: Private customers adopting Runtime LTS want an easy/explicit way to pin LTS runtime artifacts and a safer default monitoring posture for the slower-change channel. This PR adds Helm values for selecting LTS runtime image tags and turns on a recommended set of alerts when the LTS channel is enabled (without changing defaults for non-LTS installs).

What changed: 1) Introduced a small, explicit LTS selection surface in values.yaml: `runtime.channel` (default: "stable"), and `runtime.lts.tag` (optional) to pin the exact runtime image tag when `runtime.channel=lts`. `runtime.image.tag` continues to work as an escape hatch in all modes, but the chart will prefer `runtime.lts.tag` when channel=lts to reduce footguns. 2) Added `observability.ltsDefaults.enabled` (default: true when channel=lts; false otherwise) which enables a curated set of PrometheusRule alerts and dashboards wiring recommended by SRE for LTS patch operations (canary + rollback). 3) Updated NOTES.txt and chart README snippets to document the recommended LTS install command and how to override tags.

Behavior details: - Default behavior is unchanged unless a user opts into LTS via `runtime.channel: lts` (or sets `observability.ltsDefaults.enabled: true`). - When `runtime.channel=lts`, and `runtime.lts.tag` is unset, we keep existing tag resolution (whatever `runtime.image.tag` resolves to) but log a Helm NOTES warning nudging users to pin an explicit LTS tag for auditability. - Alerting rules are scoped to the runtime deployment and will not fire unless Prometheus is installed and `observability.prometheusRules.enabled=true`.

Alerts included under LTS defaults (initial set, intentionally conservative): - Runtime pod crashloop / high restart rate - 5xx / request error-rate burn (short window) - p95 latency above SLO threshold (configurable) - GPU OOM / CUDA out-of-memory errors (via log-based metric hook if enabled) - Scheduler queue depth sustained high (when metric is present)

Why now: This is a dependency for the Runtime LTS pilot so that the Private installer/upgrade guide can recommend a single, consistent approach for pinning runtime-1.20-lts.* artifacts and turning on the standard LTS rollout/rollback alert coverage.

Example values: `runtime: { channel: lts, lts: { tag: "runtime-1.20-lts.0" } }` and `observability: { prometheusRules: { enabled: true } }`.

Testing: - `helm lint` for all charts - `helm template` smoke renders for channel=stable and channel=lts - chart unit tests updated for tag resolution precedence - validated with a local Kind cluster + kube-prometheus-stack (alerts loaded, no immediate firing on idle)

Follow-ups (out of scope here): - wiring alert thresholds to the SRE LTS regression-gates doc defaults (will land in Private playbook + values examples) - additional alert tuning once we have canary data from the first LTS RC

Refs: ENG-4829 (Private installer compatibility), ENG-4828 (LTS release runbook), SUP-3921 (customer request for stable line + clearer operational posture).
commits: charts: add runtime.channel and runtime.lts.tag values + template precedence
observability: add ltsDefaults toggle and recommended PrometheusRule set
docs: update README/NOTES with LTS install + pinning guidance
tests: update chart tests for LTS tag resolution
review_conversation:
Sean Gallagher (SRE) 2026-01-15: The direction looks right, but I’d like the LTS alerts to be opt-out only when channel=lts. If a customer flips to LTS and forgets to enable rules, we lose the safety net. Can you make `observability.ltsDefaults.enabled` default to true when channel=lts and leave stable behavior unchanged?

Sahana Iyer (author) 2026-01-15: Yep. I’ll make ltsDefaults conditional on runtime.channel and keep the top-level `prometheusRules.enabled` gate as-is. Also adding a NOTES warning when channel=lts but prometheusRules disabled.

Miles Thornton 2026-01-16: For rollback, we care about restart-rate + error-rate + p95. Please ensure those rules exist even if GPU metrics aren’t present (GPU metrics are cluster-dependent). Also, can you namespace labels so multi-release installs don’t collide?

Sahana Iyer 2026-01-16: Ack. The core rules don’t require GPU metrics; the OOM one is conditional on the metric existing. Updated PrometheusRule labels to include release name and chart.

Vivek Kulkarni 2026-01-17: From the Private product side: we need a very clear pinning path that matches runtime version semantics (`runtime-1.20-lts.0`, etc.). Can we avoid overloading `runtime.image.tag` and instead document the dedicated LTS tag value as the recommended path?

Sahana Iyer 2026-01-17: Done. README now recommends `runtime.lts.tag` when channel=lts; `runtime.image.tag` stays as an escape hatch.

Allison Grant 2026-01-18: Please add a short note on how to override latency threshold. Also make sure the alert queries don’t hardcode metric names that differ between Hosted and Private.

Sahana Iyer 2026-01-18: Added `observability.alerts.latencyP95ThresholdMs` and kept queries against the Private runtime histogram metric (`redwood_runtime_request_latency_ms_bucket`). If a cluster uses a different prefix, they can override rule expressions via `observability.prometheusRules.extraRules`.

Connor O'Brien 2026-01-20: Looks good. Please squash on merge and include a release note line for the Private installer team.

Sean Gallagher 2026-01-20: Approved after the defaulting change + NOTES warning. Thanks.
merge_outcome: Merged (squash) by Connor O'Brien into main
release_notes: Private Helm charts: add `runtime.channel=lts` and `runtime.lts.tag` for pinning Runtime LTS image tags.
When LTS channel is enabled, recommended runtime alerts are enabled by default (opt-out) to support canary/rollback operations.
